FN-CY2MQQ-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator April Weaver
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/19/2023
Senate Bill 57 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education will establish
the Alabama Loan Repayment Program for Nursing Education students who agree to work in a
prelicense nursing education program in the state for 2 years. The loans will be administered by
the Alabama Board of Nursing and funded by direct appropriation from the Education Trust
Fund. The Board may award three year scholarships for recipients pursuing a master degree and
four year scholarships for recipients pursuing a doctorate degree. First year annual loan amounts
may not exceed $15,000 but may be increased annually by no more than 5% in years 2-3 for
recipients pursing a master’s degree and years 2-4 for recipients pursing a doctorate degree. This
bill also provides for the repayment of the nursing education loans and penalties for
non-fulfillment of loan contracts and for the repeal of the program effective September 30,
2029, unless extended by an act of the Legislature.
This bill will increase the administrative obligations of the Board by an undetermined amount
(1) for the administration of the loan repayment program; (2) to adopt reasonable rules to
implement and administer the program; (3) to report annually on the condition and
accomplishments of the program; and (4) to work with the Alabama Commission on Evaluation
Services (ACES) to develop, track, and collect performance metrics data and other measures of
success to include in the annual report required pursuant to this bill.

FN-CY2MQQ-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator April Weaver
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 05/09/2023
Senate Bill 57 as passed the Senate would establish the Alabama Loan Repayment Program for
Nursing Education, to be administered by the Alabama Board of Nursing and funded by direct
appropriation from the Education Trust Fund, to award loans to certain students who agree to
work in a prelicense nursing education program in the state.
Regarding this program, this bill would provide: (1) that the Board may award three-year loans
for recipients pursuing a master degree and four-year loans for recipients pursuing a doctorate
degree; (2) the maximum annual loan amounts for the first year of the program may not exceed
$15,000 but may be increased annually by no more than 5%; (3) for terms of loan repayment and
penalties for non-fulfillment of loan contracts; and (4) for the repeal of the program on
September 30, 2029, unless extended by an act of the Legislature.
This bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Board to: (1) administer the loan
repayment program, including the adoption of rules for the program; (2) produce an annual
report on the program; and (3) to consult with the Alabama Commission on Evaluation Services
(ACES) to develop performance metrics data and other measures of success to include in the
annual report required pursuant to this bill. This bill would also increase the administrative
obligations of ACES to evaluate the program in Fiscal Year 2028.
